svg.title: Fig 5 — Turret positioning and torque budget (why there is no detent)
svg.desc: A: S1 pulse versus time with a −50 µs overshoot so the final approach is always upward, and a tooth sketch showing the same flank always driving. B: error budget at R55 against the ±3.0 mm pocket capture. C: torque at the S1 horn versus stall, with the rejected v2.0 designs as ghost bars. D: holding when idle by friction and the gearbox.
svg.text: Fig 5 — Turret positioning and torque budget (why there is no detent)
S1 alone positions the turret: a one-direction approach makes backlash repeatable, the error stack fits the pocket capture, and the torque budget leaves no room for a detent or a slot crossing.

g.text: If the target is lower: go to target − 50 µs, then up. S1 stays powered until the disc is back at REST.
pocket capture: mouth 22 mm − vial 16 mm → ±3.0 mm
The 1.5 × 45° pocket chamfers funnel the vial in; no detent is needed to centre the column.
Slot crossing: 79 + 45 × 2 / 0.9 ≈ 179 (dip 3.7 mm, climb ratio 1.10). Detent: needs 202 > 177–181 stall.

Friction + gearbox hold the column; nothing
is pushing it, so it stays over the disc.
Power loss: a key opens the hatch and the
turret turns by hand (≈1 N); key use is logged.
ENV-2 ◐ — positive lock / brake = product path
No detent: holding comes from friction and the gear train, positioning from S1.
